VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a solid fundamental picture with improving trajectory. Q1 2026 showed revenue of $34.44B (+2.9% YoY), EPS of $1.20 (+4.3% YoY), and record adjusted EBITDA of $13.4B (+6.7% YoY). The company achieved its first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds since 2013 (55K), raised full-year EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99, and generated $3.8B in free cash flow (+4% YoY). Operating margins improved to 21.2% and ROE expanded to 17% from ~10.5% a year ago, reflecting the Frontier acquisition integration and cost transformation benefits. The balance sheet shows $104.6B in equity against $313.3B in liabilities, with management targeting 2.0x net debt/EBITDA by 2027. On valuation, the stock trades at a P/E of 11.1x, which is at the absolute low end of its 11.1-21.2x range over the past year and well below the ~17-18x average, suggesting significant discounting. The 6% dividend yield with 20 consecutive years of increases and a $25B buyback authorization provide strong shareholder return support. Near-term catalysts include upcoming investor conference presentations (MoffettNathanson May 13, JPM May 18) where management can reinforce the positive narrative, and continued execution on the $21.5B+ full-year FCF target. Risks include elevated 10-year Treasury yields (4.47%) pressuring dividend stock valuations, heavy debt load (~$120B), and competitive pressure from T-Mobile's broadband push. The satellite-to-cell joint venture with AT&T and T-Mobile is a modest positive for rural coverage but not a material near-term catalyst. Overall, improving fundamentals at a historically low valuation with a credible near-term guidance raise trajectory supports a mildly-to-moderately attractive rating.
